Who Told Us What, and When

The notes, advice and contacts behind Dad's current help in one place.

Download PDF

A therapist said something about the stairs back in the spring. Your sister remembers it one way and you remember it another, and the note, if anyone made one, could be in three different places.

This page doesn't ask you to work out what any of it means. It asks where each thing is, how old it is, and who has it.

What to collectWhere it isIts dateWho has it
The family's notes on an ordinary week for Dad
The list of needs and open questions from the earlier step, if you made one
Anything his doctor has said or written about help he needs now
Anything a therapist has said or written about how he gets around
Anything a professional has confirmed about how often or when help is needed
Notes on what helps him hear, see and keep in touch
Who helps Dad, with what, and their phone numbers
What each helper has said they can keep doing
His doctors, his pharmacy, and any nurse or therapist he sees, with phone numbers
The family's lists of essentials and preferences, if they've been started
Questions nobody has answered yet, and who each one is for

Scroll sideways to see every column, or print this page to fill it in.

What's missing, and who will ask for it

Anything above with an empty line, or a date nobody is sure of. Put a name next to each. There's no deadline.

For example Nothing in writing about the stairs. Tracy will ask the therapist's office what was noted, and when.

How to use it

  • Write the date each thing was said or written. If nobody is sure, write “undated” and note who remembers it.
  • Where something was said aloud and never written down, note who heard it. If two people remember it differently, write both.
  • Don't rewrite or summarize a document here. Just say where it is.
  • Take this page to Dad's next routine appointment, so anything undated can be checked with the person who said it.

What this page doesn't do

It doesn't explain what any note or piece of advice means, and it doesn't say whether something said last spring still holds. Those are questions for the person who said it.

Where this comes from

The contacts row follows the CDC's care-plan guidance, which lists health care providers and their contact information among the things to keep in one place. The rest come from the Family Care Roadmap's working list for this step.
